title: Presheaf inverse image of modules is left adjoint to direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces, $\mathcal O$ a presheaf of commutative rings on $Y$, and let $f_p$, $f_*$ and the unit $i_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to f_*f_p\mathcal G$ of the adjunction $f_p\dashv f_*$ on presheaves of sets, abelian groups and commutative rings be as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), with $f_p\mathcal G(U)=\varinjlim_{V\supseteq f(U)}\mathcal G(V)$ and coprojections $\iota^U_V$. (1) For a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], there is a unique map $f_p\mathcal O(U)\times f_p\mathcal G(U)\to f_p\mathcal G(U)$ for every open $U\subseteq X$ with $\iota^U_V(a)\cdot\iota^U_V(g)=\iota^U_V(ag)$ for all $V\supseteq f(U)$, $a\in\mathcal O(V)$, $g\in\mathcal G(V)$; it makes the presheaf of abelian groups $f_p\mathcal G$ a presheaf of $f_p\mathcal O$-modules, and for a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules $u$, $f_pu$ is $f_p\mathcal O$-linear. (2) For a presheaf of $f_p\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F$ on $X$, the presheaf of abelian groups $f_*\mathcal F$, $V\mapsto\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)$, is a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules with $a\in\mathcal O(V)$ acting on $\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)$ through $i_{\mathcal O,V}(a)\in f_p\mathcal O(f^{-1}V)$; for a morphism of presheaves of $f_p\mathcal O$-modules $w$, $f_*w$ is $\mathcal O$-linear. (3) The bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PAb}(X)}(f_p\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PAb}(Y)}(\mathcal G,f_*\mathcal F)$, $\psi\mapsto f_*\psi\circ i_{\mathcal G}$, of the adjunction $f_p\dashv f_*$ on presheaves of abelian groups maps the $f_p\mathcal O$-linear morphisms exactly onto the $\mathcal O$-linear ones, and so restricts to a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(f_p\mathcal O)}(f_p\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal G,f_*\mathcal F)$, natural in $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Tag 008T, lemma-pullback-presheaf-module (line 2727), for (1); Tag 008S, lemma-pushforward-presheaf-module (line 2693), for the f_*f_pO-module structure in (2); Tag 008U, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-presheaves-modules (line 2782), for (3), whose proof leaves to the reader that i_G and c_F are module maps

proof.text: *Step 1 (elements of $f_p\mathcal O(U)$ and $f_p\mathcal G(U)$).* Fix an open $U\subseteq X$ and let $I_U$ be the set of opens $V\subseteq Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, ordered by reverse inclusion; it is nonempty ($Y\in I_U$) and directed ($V,V'\in I_U\Rightarrow V\cap V'\in I_U$), so it is a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and by [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2) $f_p\mathcal G(U)$ is the colimit of $V\mapsto\mathcal G(V)$ over $I_U$ in abelian groups and $f_p\mathcal O(U)$ the colimit of $V\mapsto\mathcal O(V)$ in commutative rings, the transition maps being the restriction maps. Abelian groups are $\mathbf Z$-modules, so [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (with $R=\mathbf Z$) applies to $f_p\mathcal G(U)$, and [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] applies to $f_p\mathcal O(U)$; in the directed set $I_U$ a pair of morphisms $V\to W\leftarrow V'$ is $W\subseteq V\cap V'$ and the transition maps are restrictions, so they give: (a) every element of $f_p\mathcal O(U)$ is $\iota^U_V(a)$ for some $V\in I_U$, $a\in\mathcal O(V)$, and every element of $f_p\mathcal G(U)$ is $\iota^U_V(g)$ for some $V\in I_U$, $g\in\mathcal G(V)$; (b) $\iota^U_V(x)=\iota^U_{V'}(x')$ if and only if there is $W\in I_U$ with $W\subseteq V\cap V'$ and $x|_W=x'|_W$ (for both $\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal G$). Since $\iota^U_V=\iota^U_W\circ(-)|_W$ for $W\subseteq V$ in $I_U$ (cocone condition), any finitely many elements of $f_p\mathcal O(U)$ and of $f_p\mathcal G(U)$ can be written as $\iota^U_V(\cdot)$ with one common $V\in I_U$ (take the intersection of the indices of representatives given by (a)).

source.place: Tag 008T (lemma-pullback-presheaf-module), proof: the identification of $f_p\mathcal O(U)\times f_p\mathcal G(U)$ with $\colim_V(\mathcal O(V)\times\mathcal G(V))$, which the source takes from Categories 002W

proof.text: *Step 2 (the product of (1): existence and uniqueness).* For $x\in f_p\mathcal O(U)$, $y\in f_p\mathcal G(U)$ write $x=\iota^U_V(a)$, $y=\iota^U_V(g)$ with a common $V\in I_U$ (step 1) and put $x\cdot y=\iota^U_V(ag)$, $ag$ the product of the $\mathcal O(V)$-module $\mathcal G(V)$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. This does not depend on the choice: if also $x=\iota^U_{V'}(a')$, $y=\iota^U_{V'}(g')$, step 1 (b) gives $W_1,W_2\in I_U$ inside $V\cap V'$ with $a|_{W_1}=a'|_{W_1}$, $g|_{W_2}=g'|_{W_2}$; with $W=W_1\cap W_2\in I_U$, semilinearity of the restriction maps of $\mathcal G$ gives $(ag)|_W=a|_W\,g|_W=a'|_W\,g'|_W=(a'g')|_W$, so $\iota^U_V(ag)=\iota^U_W((ag)|_W)=\iota^U_W((a'g')|_W)=\iota^U_{V'}(a'g')$. By construction $\iota^U_V(a)\cdot\iota^U_V(g)=\iota^U_V(ag)$ for all $V\in I_U$, $a$, $g$; and any map with this property agrees with this one, since every pair $(x,y)$ is of the form $(\iota^U_V(a),\iota^U_V(g))$ by step 1.

source.place: Tag 008T, proof: the map $\colim_V(\mathcal O(V)\times\mathcal G(V))\to\colim_V\mathcal G(V)$ induced by the multiplications

proof.text: *Step 3 (the module structure and functoriality of (1)).* Given finitely many elements, represent them at one common $V\in I_U$ (step 1); since $\iota^U_V:\mathcal O(V)\to f_p\mathcal O(U)$ is a ring homomorphism (a coprojection in commutative rings) and $\iota^U_V:\mathcal G(V)\to f_p\mathcal G(U)$ is additive, each module axiom for $f_p\mathcal G(U)$ over $f_p\mathcal O(U)$ is the image under $\iota^U_V$ of the same axiom in the $\mathcal O(V)$-module $\mathcal G(V)$, e.g. $(\iota(a)+\iota(a'))\cdot\iota(g)=\iota((a+a')g)=\iota(ag+a'g)=\iota(a)\iota(g)+\iota(a')\iota(g)$, $\iota(a)(\iota(g)+\iota(g'))=\iota(ag+ag')$, $(\iota(a)\iota(a'))\iota(g)=\iota((aa')g)=\iota(a(a'g))=\iota(a)(\iota(a')\iota(g))$, $1\cdot\iota(g)=\iota(1)\iota(g)=\iota(g)$. For opens $U'\subseteq U$ the restriction map $r$ of $f_p\mathcal G$ and that of $f_p\mathcal O$ send $\iota^U_V$ to $\iota^{U'}_V$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), so $r(\iota^U_V(a)\iota^U_V(g))=\iota^{U'}_V(ag)=\iota^{U'}_V(a)\,\iota^{U'}_V(g)=r(\iota^U_V(a))\,r(\iota^U_V(g))$: the restriction maps are semilinear, and $f_p\mathcal G$ is a presheaf of $f_p\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For an $\mathcal O$-linear morphism $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$, $(f_pu)_U\circ\iota^U_V=\iota'^U_V\circ u_V$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2) gives $(f_pu)_U(\iota^U_V(a)\iota^U_V(g))=\iota'^U_V(u_V(ag))=\iota'^U_V(a\,u_V(g))=\iota^U_V(a)\cdot(f_pu)_U(\iota^U_V(g))$, so $f_pu$ is $f_p\mathcal O$-linear; $f_p$ preserves identities and composition already on presheaves of abelian groups. This is (1).

source.place: Tag 008T, proof: 'We leave it to the reader to see this is compatible with restriction mappings and defines a structure of $f_p\mathcal O$-module on $f_p\mathcal G$', and 'functorial in $\mathcal G$'

proof.text: *Step 4 (the module structure of (2)).* For $V\subseteq Y$ open, $i_{\mathcal O,V}=\iota^{f^{-1}V}_V:\mathcal O(V)\to f_p\mathcal O(f^{-1}V)$ is a ring homomorphism (a coprojection in commutative rings) [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), so the $f_p\mathcal O(f^{-1}V)$-module $\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)=f_*\mathcal F(V)$ becomes an $\mathcal O(V)$-module by $a\cdot s=i_{\mathcal O,V}(a)s$ (restriction of scalars). For $V'\subseteq V$, $a\in\mathcal O(V)$, $s\in\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)$: $(i_{\mathcal O,V}(a)s)|_{f^{-1}V'}=i_{\mathcal O,V}(a)|_{f^{-1}V'}\,s|_{f^{-1}V'}=i_{\mathcal O,V'}(a|_{V'})\,s|_{f^{-1}V'}$, by the semilinearity of the restriction maps of $\mathcal F$ over $f_p\mathcal O$ and because $i_{\mathcal O}:\mathcal O\to f_*f_p\mathcal O$ is a morphism of presheaves; so the restriction maps of $f_*\mathcal F$ are semilinear and $f_*\mathcal F$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For an $f_p\mathcal O$-linear $w:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$, $(f_*w)_V=w_{f^{-1}V}$ is $f_p\mathcal O(f^{-1}V)$-linear, hence $\mathcal O(V)$-linear for the restricted scalars. This is (2). (The source, 008S, states the $f_*f_p\mathcal O$-module structure; the $\mathcal O$-structure of 008U is its restriction along $i_{\mathcal O}$.)

source.place: Tag 008S (lemma-pushforward-presheaf-module), proof, with the restriction along $i_{\mathcal O}$ stated in Tag 008U

proof.text: *Step 5 (the abelian bijection and its formula).* By [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2) with values in abelian groups, $f_p\dashv f_*$ on presheaves of abelian groups with unit $i$; so the adjunction bijection is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PAb}(X)}(f_p\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PAb}(Y)}(\mathcal G,f_*\mathcal F)$, $\psi\mapsto\varphi=f_*\psi\circ i_{\mathcal G}$, natural in $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F$; on sections $\varphi_V=\psi_{f^{-1}V}\circ\iota^{f^{-1}V}_V$. For $V\in I_U$ (i.e. $U\subseteq f^{-1}V$) the restriction $f_p\mathcal G(f^{-1}V)\to f_p\mathcal G(U)$ sends $\iota^{f^{-1}V}_V$ to $\iota^U_V$ and $\psi$ commutes with restrictions, hence $(\ast)$ $\psi_U\circ\iota^U_V=\rho_{U}\circ\varphi_V$, where $\rho_U:\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)\to\mathcal F(U)$ is the restriction of $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Tag 008U, proof: 'the correspondence is determined by the rule $\psi\mapsto f_*\psi\circ i_{\mathcal G}$'

proof.text: *Step 6 (linear $\psi$ gives linear $\varphi$).* The unit $i_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to f_*f_p\mathcal G$ is $\mathcal O$-linear for the $\mathcal O$-structure of step 4 on $f_*(f_p\mathcal G)$ (with $f_p\mathcal G$ the $f_p\mathcal O$-module of step 3): $i_{\mathcal G,V}(ag)=\iota^{f^{-1}V}_V(ag)=\iota^{f^{-1}V}_V(a)\,\iota^{f^{-1}V}_V(g)=i_{\mathcal O,V}(a)\cdot i_{\mathcal G,V}(g)$ by the defining property of the product (step 2, with $U=f^{-1}V$). If $\psi$ is $f_p\mathcal O$-linear, $f_*\psi$ is $\mathcal O$-linear by step 4, so $\varphi=f_*\psi\circ i_{\mathcal G}$ is $\mathcal O$-linear as a composite of $\mathcal O$-linear maps of presheaves of modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

source.place: Tag 008U, proof: 'it suffices to check that the maps $i_{\mathcal G}$ ... are compatible with module structures, which we leave to the reader' (the $i_{\mathcal G}$ half)

proof.text: *Step 7 (linear $\varphi$ gives linear $\psi$).* Let $\varphi=f_*\psi\circ i_{\mathcal G}$ be $\mathcal O$-linear, $U\subseteq X$ open, $x\in f_p\mathcal O(U)$, $y\in f_p\mathcal G(U)$. By step 1 (a) and the common-index remark there are $V\in I_U$, $a\in\mathcal O(V)$, $g\in\mathcal G(V)$ with $x=\iota^U_V(a)$, $y=\iota^U_V(g)$ ([lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]). Then, by step 2, $(\ast)$ of step 5, the $\mathcal O$-linearity of $\varphi$ (step 4 structure), the semilinearity of the restriction $\rho_U$ of $\mathcal F$ over $f_p\mathcal O$, and $\iota^{f^{-1}V}_V(a)|_U=\iota^U_V(a)$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2): $\psi_U(xy)=\psi_U(\iota^U_V(ag))=\rho_U(\varphi_V(ag))=\rho_U(i_{\mathcal O,V}(a)\,\varphi_V(g))=\iota^U_V(a)\,\rho_U(\varphi_V(g))=x\,\psi_U(\iota^U_V(g))=x\,\psi_U(y)$. With additivity, $\psi_U$ is $f_p\mathcal O(U)$-linear for every $U$, so $\psi$ is $f_p\mathcal O$-linear [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. (The source checks instead that the counit $c_{\mathcal F}:f_pf_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is linear and uses $\psi=c_{\mathcal F}\circ f_p\varphi$; the counit is not stated in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], and the computation above, which is that check composed with $f_p\varphi$, uses only the unit.)

source.place: Tag 008U, proof: the $c_{\mathcal F}$ half of 'compatible with module structures, which we leave to the reader', with the colimit formula of Tag 008T

proof.text: *Step 8 (the restricted bijection; naturality).* By steps 6 and 7 the bijection of step 5 maps the set of $f_p\mathcal O$-linear morphisms $f_p\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ onto the set of $\mathcal O$-linear morphisms $\mathcal G\to f_*\mathcal F$, so it restricts to a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(f_p\mathcal O)}(f_p\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal G,f_*\mathcal F)$ (a bijection restricted to a subset $A$ with image exactly $B$ is a bijection $A\to B$). Naturality: for $\mathcal O$-linear $u:\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G$ and $f_p\mathcal O$-linear $w:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$, $f_pu$ and $f_*w$ are linear by steps 3 and 4, and the naturality identities $f_*(w\circ\psi\circ f_pu)\circ i_{\mathcal G'}=f_*w\circ(f_*\psi\circ i_{\mathcal G})\circ u$ hold in presheaves of abelian groups by step 5; since morphisms of presheaves of modules are morphisms of presheaves of abelian groups with a property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], they hold for the restricted bijection. This is (3).

source.place: Tag 008U, statement and proof: 'what we have to prove is that under this correspondence, the subsets of module maps correspond'
